Let \( A_1, A_2, A_3, \ldots \) be a sequence of finite nonempty sets of positive integers. Given that \( |A_i \cap A_j| = \gcd(i, j) \) for all (not necessarily distinct) positive integers \( i \) and \( j \), compute the minimum possible value of

\[
\sum_{d|250} \max A_d,
\]

where the sum ranges over all positive integer divisors \( d \) of 250.

(For a finite nonempty set \( S \), we define \( \max S \) as the largest element of \( S \).)


Put your final answer within \boxed{}.

Let \(\varphi\) denote Euler’s totient function, with the convention \(\varphi(1)=1\).

First, determine the forced structure of the sets.

Since \(i=j\) gives
\[
|A_i|=i,
\]
and if \(i\mid j\) then
\[
|A_i\cap A_j|=\gcd(i,j)=i=|A_i|,
\]
we get
\[
i\mid j \implies A_i\subseteq A_j.
\]
Thus for all \(i,j\),
\[
A_i\cap A_j=A_{\gcd(i,j)}.
\]

Now take any positive integer \(x\) that belongs to at least one \(A_i\). Let
\[
S_x=\{i\in \mathbb Z_{>0}:x\in A_i\}.
\]
If \(i\in S_x\) and \(i\mid j\), then \(x\in A_j\), so \(S_x\) is upward closed under divisibility. Also, if \(i,j\in S_x\), then
\[
x\in A_i\cap A_j=A_{\gcd(i,j)},
\]
so \(S_x\) is closed under taking gcds. Let \(g\) be the smallest element of \(S_x\). If \(m\in S_x\) and \(g\nmid m\), then \(\gcd(g,m)\in S_x\) and is a positive divisor of \(g\) strictly smaller than \(g\), contradiction. Hence \(g\mid m\) for all \(m\in S_x\), and upward closure gives the converse. Therefore \(x\in A_i\) if and only if \(g\mid i\).

So each element belongs to a unique “class” \(h\): it belongs exactly to all sets \(A_i\) with \(h\mid i\). Let \(E_h\) be the set of elements whose class is \(h\). Then
\[
A_i=\bigcup_{h\mid i}E_h
\]
disjointly. Hence
\[
i=|A_i|=\sum_{h\mid i}|E_h|
\]
for every positive integer \(i\). By Möbius inversion,
\[
|E_h|=\varphi(h).
\]

Now only the divisors of \(250\) matter. The divisors are
\[
1,2,5,10,25,50,125,250,
\]
with corresponding class sizes
\[
1,1,4,4,20,20,100,100.
\]

For each divisor \(h\mid 250\), let
\[
M_h=\max E_h.
\]
Then for each divisor \(d\mid 250\),
\[
\max A_d=\max_{h\mid d} M_h.
\]

Sort the eight numbers \(M_h\) in nondecreasing order:
\[
m_1\le m_2\le \cdots \le m_8,
\]
and let \(h_r\) be the corresponding divisor. Write
\[
w_r=\varphi(h_r),\qquad W_r=w_1+\cdots+w_r.
\]
The first \(r\) classes contain \(W_r\) distinct positive integers, all at most \(m_r\), so
\[
W_r\le m_r.
\]

For each \(r=1,\dots,8\), let \(N_r\) be the number of divisors \(d\mid 250\) that are multiples of at least one of
\[
h_r,h_{r+1},\dots,h_8.
\]
Then \(N_1\ge N_2\ge \cdots \ge N_8\), and since each \(h_i\) is itself a divisor of \(250\),
\[
N_r\ge 8-r+1=9-r.
\]

Using the layer-cake identity,
\[
\sum_{d\mid 250}\max A_d
=\sum_{t\ge 1}\#\{d\mid 250:\max A_d\ge t\}.
\]
Grouping \(t\) by the intervals \((m_{r-1},m_r]\), with \(m_0=0\), gives
\[
\sum_{d\mid 250}\max A_d
=\sum_{r=1}^8 (m_r-m_{r-1})N_r.
\]
Equivalently, setting \(N_9=0\),
\[
\sum_{d\mid 250}\max A_d
=\sum_{r=1}^8 m_r(N_r-N_{r+1}).
\]
Since \(N_r\ge N_{r+1}\) and \(m_r\ge W_r\),
\[
\sum_{d\mid 250}\max A_d
\ge \sum_{r=1}^8 W_r(N_r-N_{r+1})
=\sum_{r=1}^8 (W_r-W_{r-1})N_r
=\sum_{r=1}^8 w_rN_r.
\]
Thus
\[
\sum_{d\mid 250}\max A_d
\ge \sum_{r=1}^8 w_r(9-r).
\]
The numbers \(w_r\) are a permutation of
\[
1,1,4,4,20,20,100,100.
\]
The coefficients \(9-r\) are
\[
8,7,6,5,4,3,2,1,
\]
so by the rearrangement inequality the minimum occurs when the \(w_r\) are increasing:
\[
1,1,4,4,20,20,100,100.
\]
Therefore
\[
\sum_{d\mid 250}\max A_d
\ge 1\cdot8+1\cdot7+4\cdot6+4\cdot5+20\cdot4+20\cdot3+100\cdot2+100\cdot1=499.
\]

It remains to show that \(499\) is attainable.

For each positive integer \(h\) and each \(1\le a\le \varphi(h)\), introduce a distinct positive integer \(x_{h,a}\). Define
\[
A_n=\{x_{h,a}:h\mid n\}.
\]
Then
\[
|A_i\cap A_j|
=
\left|\{x_{h,a}:h\mid \gcd(i,j)\}\right|
=
\sum_{h\mid \gcd(i,j)}\varphi(h)
=
\gcd(i,j),
\]
so the construction is valid.

Assign labels as follows:
\[
\begin{aligned}
E_1 &: 1,\\
E_2 &: 2,\\
E_5 &: 3,4,5,6,\\
E_{10} &: 7,8,9,10,\\
E_{25} &: 11,\dots,30,\\
E_{50} &: 31,\dots,50,\\
E_{125} &: 51,\dots,150,\\
E_{250} &: 151,\dots,250.
\end{aligned}
\]
All other elements \(E_h\) with \(h\nmid 250\) may be given distinct labels greater than \(250\).

For the divisors of \(250\), the maxima are:
\[
\begin{aligned}
\max A_1&=1,\\
\max A_2&=2,\\
\max A_5&=6,\\
\max A_{10}&=10,\\
\max A_{25}&=30,\\
\max A_{50}&=50,\\
\max A_{125}&=150,\\
\max A_{250}&=250.
\end{aligned}
\]
Their sum is
\[
1+2+6+10+30+50+150+250=499.
\]

Hence the minimum possible value is

\[
\boxed{499}
\]
